newsitem.title: UK: Siemens move to prepare debt for EMU well received.
newsitem.headline: Siemens move to prepare debt for EMU well received.

text.p: German electronics and engineering giant Siemens's euro Eurobond had all the right components to make it a huge success and sparked a great response, syndicate officials said on Tuesday.

"The deal has been a huge success," a syndicate manager at joint lead manager J.P. Morgan said. "All three deals are fully sold and comfortably so. No paper has come back and people are still looking for more."
"We increased both the mark and French franc tranches and could have increased the guilder tranche, but Siemens had a 2.0 billion mark ceiling."
Christian Weller von Alefeld, head of treasury at Siemens Munich, told Reuters Financial Television on Tuesday he felt the single currency would go ahead.
"And with that (euro) we will be able to redenominate our French franc, guilder and mark issue, reconsolidate and have a liquid corporate benchmark Eurobond."

He said current interest rate levels for 10-year funding were very attractive. "The 10-year range is not always a window that is open in the Eurobond market and the spread levels we obtained are attractive."
J.P. Morgan said Siemens was looking ahead to the post-EMU market and wanted to position itself but said the tranches still had to work on a stand alone basis.

Syndicate managers at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (joint lead manager on all tranches), Paribas (joint lead on the French franc tranche) and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett (joint lead on the guilder tranche) echoed J.P. Morgan's view.
Siemens was the first company to prepare its international long-term debt for a single European currency.

It has not issued a syndicated fixed-income deal publicly for more than 25 years. Dealers away from the leads said the purpose of euro Eurobond issues has been to alert investors to new or infrequent borrowers as much as to raise funds.
"The scarcity value, the magic triple-A for a corporate and the euro fungibility clause are all the right components to make it a tremendous success," a Paribas syndicate manager said.
The three-tranche 10-year bond offering was launched in French francs, guilders and marks totalling almost 2.0 billion marks (around one billion Ecu).

All three deals, each paying a coupon of 5.50 percent, will be redenominated in euros after European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) after which they will be fungible and merged to create a jumbo euro Eurobond.
The 750 million mark tranche, launched at 17 basis points yield spread over Bunds, reflected the demand with the spread tightening three notches.
The 500 million guilder tranche tightened in one notch to trade at 19 b.p. over while the 2.5 billion French franc tranche held its 14 b.p. over spread.
J.P. Morgan said distribution of the deals was broad with a strong bid for the mark tranche from London, Switzerland and into Germany, France, Benelux, Austria, Italy, and the Middle and Far East.
Paribas said one-third of the French franc paper sold to French institutional investors, with the rest selling to Asian and European investors.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett syndicate manager said 75 percent of the guilder paper went to Dutch institutional investors with the rest being sold to European institutional investors.
J.P. Morgan said they were looking at other transactions with potential for euro-redenomination.
